source_text: De eo quod scriptum est: Servivit populus Domino omnibus diebus Iesu et omnibus diebus seniorum qui viderunt opera Domini. Lector legebat timuit; nos habemus servivit. Unusquisque sibi praestat dies Iesu vel dies impiorum. Si lumen verum illuminat animam et sol iustitiae oritur, habemus dies Iesu dies salutis. Si lucem exstinguibilem recipimus, dies mali Manasse vel Pharaonis. In diebus Achaz impii Esaias Dominum videre non potuit donec mortuus est rex nequam.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning that which written is: Served people Lord all days of-Jesus and all days of-elders who saw works of-Lord. Reader was-reading feared; we have served. Each-one for-himself provides days of-Jesus or days of-impious. If light true illuminates soul and sun of-justice rises, we-have days of-Jesus days of-salvation. If light extinguishable we-receive, days evil of-Manasseh or of-Pharaoh. In days of-Ahaz of-impious Isaiah Lord to-see not could until dead is king wicked.
pass_b_english: On what is written: [[The people served the Lord all the days of Jesus and all the days of the elders who had seen the Lord’s great works >> Bible:Judges 2:7]]. The lector read “feared”; we have “served.” Each of us makes for himself either Jesus’ days or the wicked’s days. If [[the true light that enlightens everyone >> Bible:John 1:9]] lights the soul and [[the sun of righteousness >> Bible:Malachi 4:2]] rises, we have Jesus’ days — days of salvation. If we take an extinguishable light, we have evil days of Manasseh or Pharaoh. In wicked Ahaz’s days Isaiah could not see the Lord until that bad king died.
